t: None of the funds available under this Act may be used to carry out proposed revenue procedure 4830–01–M of the Internal Revenue Service entitled “Proposed Revenue Procedure on Private Tax-Exempt Schools” (44 F.R. 9451 through 9455, February 13, 1979, F.R. Document 79–4801), and proposed revenue procedure 4830–01 of the Internal Revenue Service entitled “Proposed Revenue Procedure on Private Tax-Exempt Schools” (43 F.R. 37296 through 37298, August 22, 1978, F.R. Document 78–23515), or parts thereof.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that references to "proposed" revenue procedures published in the Federal Register imply a notice-and-comment process. The section is only an appropriations rider barring the use of funds to carry out those procedures. It does not require or authorize rulemaking, a comment period, a hearing, consultation with outside parties, or any right to sue.
fable.s: None of the funds available under this Act may be used to carry out proposed revenue procedure 4830–01–M of the Internal Revenue Service

qwen_block.w: This section is a funding restriction that prohibits the use of appropriated funds to implement specific IRS revenue procedures. It does not establish any mechanism for outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) to consult with, advise, or participate in federal decision-making. The mention of 'proposed' revenue procedures refers to the status of the IRS rules themselves, not a public comment period or advisory process mandated by this specific statutory text.
qwen_block.s: None of the funds available under this Act may be used to carry out proposed revenue procedure 4830–01–M of the Internal Revenue Service entitled “Proposed Revenue Procedure on Private Tax-Exempt Schools”

opus.w: This is a limit on appropriations that stops the IRS from spending funds to carry out certain proposed revenue procedures. It might look like participation because it cites proposed rules published in the Federal Register. But the section itself requires no comment period, hearing, consultation or other role for people outside the federal government. It only blocks spending.
opus.s: None of the funds available under this Act may be used to carry out proposed revenue procedure 4830–01–M of the Internal Revenue Service

qwen_chat.w: This section is a funding restriction that prohibits the use of appropriated funds to implement specific proposed revenue procedures. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties. The mention of 'proposed' procedures is merely identifying the subject of the ban, not invoking the procedural requirements of rulemaking or public participation.
qwen_chat.s: None of the funds available under this Act may be used to carry out proposed revenue procedure 4830–01–M of the Internal Revenue Service entitled “Proposed Revenue Procedure on Private Tax-Exempt Schools”
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the text references "Proposed Revenue Procedure," it implies a rulemaking process that typically involves public comment. However, the section itself does not mandate, describe, or require any participation; it merely prohibits the use of funds to implement specific proposed procedures. The reference to the Federal Register citations is descriptive of the procedures being banned, not an instruction to engage in the rulemaking process or consult with outsiders.
